name: Voxelotor
route_note: oral tablets or tablets for suspension once daily (withdrawn 2024)

discovery.note: An aldehyde that forms a reversible Schiff base with the N-terminal valine of the haemoglobin alpha chain, stabilising the oxygenated state.

tagline: Sickle haemoglobin polymerisation inhibitor withdrawn in 2024 over safety concerns
summary: Voxelotor binds haemoglobin and increases its oxygen affinity, preventing deoxygenated sickle haemoglobin from polymerising. It received accelerated approval in 2019 for sickle cell disease based on haemoglobin increases, but Pfizer withdrew it worldwide in 2024 after data showed more vaso-occlusive crises and deaths.
mechanism: Sickle haemoglobin (HbS) polymerises when deoxygenated, distorting red cells into rigid sickle shapes that haemolyse and block small vessels.

Voxelotor covalently and reversibly binds the N-terminal valine of the alpha-globin chain, shifting the oxygen dissociation curve to the left and keeping haemoglobin in the oxygenated, non-polymerising state. This reduced haemolysis and raised haemoglobin, although tighter oxygen binding could also reduce oxygen delivery to tissues.
uses: Sickle cell disease in patients aged four and older (approval withdrawn 2024)

history.title: Early trials
history.detail: Phase 1/2 studies of GBT440 show reduced haemolysis and higher haemoglobin.

history.title: HOPE trial
history.detail: 51% of patients on 1500 mg reach a haemoglobin rise of more than 1 g/dL versus 7% on placebo.

history.title: Accelerated approval
history.detail: FDA grants accelerated approval as Oxbryta for patients aged 12 and older.

history.title: Paediatric use
history.detail: FDA extends accelerated approval to children aged 4 to 11.

history.title: EU approval and Pfizer
history.detail: The EU grants conditional authorisation; Pfizer acquires Global Blood Therapeutics.

history.title: Worldwide withdrawal
history.detail: Pfizer withdraws voxelotor from all markets after an imbalance in vaso-occlusive crises and fatal events in post-marketing trials; EMA suspends the authorisation.

pk.half_life: about 35.5 hours in sickle cell disease
pk.bioavailability: well absorbed; extensive partitioning into red cells

serious: increased vaso-occlusive crises and deaths in post-marketing studies

facts: Voxelotor interferes with HPLC measurement of haemoglobin subtypes because it binds haemoglobin.
